To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a new tunable transmission line (TTL) structure for wideband mm-wave phase shifting, and we implement a 79° tuning range phase shifter based on this structure that occupies 35% less space than a previously reported phase shifter based upon a different tunable transmission line.

a tunable transmission line based on an inverted stripline-like structure can be used for mm-wave phase shift applications, and that it achieves a better performance than the previously reported tunable transmission line.

the phase shifters presented in this work achieve 1) the best area-efficiency, 2) best phase-shift tuning range, 3) best phase shift linearity, and 4) best phase shift accuracy among all the reported mm-wave phase shift solutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of tunable transmission lines for mm-wave phase shifers.
the development of mm-wave phase shift networks based on tunable transmission lines, and the demonstration of a wideband mm-wave phase shifer for massive hybrid MIM0 applications.
the design, modeling and characterization of tunable transmission line structures, which are key building blocks in mm-wave phased array systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented phase shifter achieves a good balance between area occupied and performance.
the proposed phase shifter achieves a better trade-off between phase shift tuning range and insertion loss than the reference phase shifter.
the proposed structure can achieve a better balance between phase shift tuning range and occupied area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed and demonstrated the first tunable transmission line with constant impedance, which is a key step towards the development of a mm-wave phase shift array with constant beamforming gain.
the proposed tunable transmission line can provide a better tradeoff between area, insertion loss, and phase shift tuning range compared to the previously-reported tunable line structure.
we have demonstrated a tunable transmission line based phase shifter which has a constant impedance and a wideband frequency operation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inverted stripline-like structure is a promising alternative to the previously-reported tunable line structure.
the constant-impedence tunable transmission line approach can provide a good alternative to previously-reported approaches for realizing mm-wave phase shift arrays.
the inverted stripline-like transmission line is a promising candidate for mm-wave phase shifting and beamforming applications.
